summary: Material changes: Taiwan August export orders reached a record $103.0 billion, up 71.4% y/y and above the verifiable Reuters consensus of +63.6%, led by AI/HPC/cloud demand. Hormuz physical traffic deteriorated to two reported commodity-vessel crossings on September 21 and two vessels were reported struck in separate incidents, while Iran offered a conditional seven-day reopening path and Saudi Arabia partially restarted its East-West Pipeline.

key_drivers.name: Taiwan August export orders exceed $100 billion for first time
key_drivers.observed: MOEA data reported by Reuters show August export orders rose 71.4% y/y to $103.0 billion versus a verifiable analyst expectation of +63.6% and July's +61.9%. Telecom orders rose 100.5% y/y and electronic products 83.9%; U.S. orders rose 88.9%.
key_drivers.interpretation: The release strengthens evidence of broad AI/HPC/cloud demand and Taiwan's semiconductor/server supply-chain momentum without directly changing company Fair Value inputs.

key_drivers.name: Hormuz traffic falls to two and two vessels reported struck
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported preliminary data showing two commodity-vessel crossings on September 21 versus 10 a day earlier and roughly 125 large commercial vessels daily before the conflict. Marisks reported separate strikes on a crude tanker and LPG tanker; both continued and responsibility remains unconfirmed.
key_drivers.interpretation: Physical shipping and marine-insurance risk worsened despite ongoing workarounds; attribution is not inferred.

key_drivers.name: Saudi East-West Pipeline partially restarts while Iran offers conditional Hormuz reopening
key_drivers.observed: Reuters sources said Saudi Arabia restarted the East-West Pipeline at a low rate, with full restoration potentially taking weeks. Separately, a senior Iranian official said Hormuz could reopen within seven days if U.S. military pressure eases and the blockade on Iranian ports is lifted.
key_drivers.interpretation: Bypass capacity and diplomatic optionality reduce the probability of a prolonged maximum oil-export constraint, but neither constitutes normalized Hormuz shipping.

key_risks: Hormuz commodity-vessel traffic remains extremely depressed and two vessels were reported struck in separate incidents, raising shipping and insurance risk.
Saudi East-West Pipeline restart is partial and full restoration may take weeks.
Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening statement is conditional on U.S. actions and is not an implemented agreement.
Russia-Ukraine energy-infrastructure attacks include the reported Moscow refinery outage, adding refined-product supply pressure.
Taiwan-specific security-policy uncertainty remains elevated ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
Fed and BOJ tightening keep global discount rates and funding costs elevated.
VIX, copper, USD/TWD and exact U.S. 2Y/10Y closes remain stale in this semantic snapshot.
